profile.baseline_state: COMPUTATIONAL CANDIDATE / ZERO EMPIRICAL SIMILARITY PASS
profile.official_summary: Persistent grapefruit; cinnamon and nutmeg heat; cardamom coolness; AOP Nyons lavender; sweet licorice; Haitian vetiver and patchouli linking rich woods.
profile.target_identity: Persistent grapefruit and a multi-temperature spice crown over floral non-camphor lavender, licorice velvet and rich ambery woods.
profile.hedonic_tension: Explosive spice-freshness versus velvety dark smoothness.
profile.authority_note: Official named naturals and accords; current label is presence evidence only, not a formula.

art_direction.primary_motif: A persistent grapefruit spear surrounded by hot cinnamon/nutmeg and cool cardamom.
art_direction.secondary_motif: A floral lavender crown sinking into sweet licorice velvet and dark polished woods.
art_direction.foreground: Grapefruit, temperature-split spice, fine lavender and licorice darkness.
art_direction.background: Patchouli-vetiver, incense, oud shadow, resin, amberwood and musk veil.
art_direction.tension: Explosive spice-freshness versus velvety dark smoothness.
art_direction.release: The sharp spear is wrapped first in lavender, then in licorice, until only a dark red trace remains in the woods.
art_direction.negative_space: Floral transmission and distributed woods stop the formula from becoming a compressed spice-amber wall.
art_direction.recurrence: Grapefruit bitterness returns late as a dry mineral edge inside licorice, vetiver and amberwood.
art_direction.texture_progression: bitter spear → hot/cool spice corona → lavender velvet → licorice lacquer → dark wood
art_direction.spatial_identity: The opening radiates in all directions; the late structure is denser, lower and more controlled.
art_direction.late_residue: Licorice, patchouli, vetiver, incense, dark oud-suede and distributed amberwood pressure.
art_direction.controlled_imperfection: A faint phenolic, bitter and smoky edge keeps the licorice from becoming candy.
art_direction.hedonic_hypothesis: The fragrance seduces through controlled danger: heat, coolness, bitterness and sweetness resolve into velvet rather than aggression.
layers: Grapefruit, methyl pamplemousse, Pamzest, bergamot, citral and aldehydes form persistent bitterness.
Cardamom, cinnamon proxy, ginger, pepper, coriander, clove traces and caraway create hot/cool motion.
Lavender, linalool, linalyl acetate, Hedione, muguet and magnolia make floral aromatic volume.
Anise, anisaldehyde, immortelle, coumarin, vanilla, benzoin, labdanum, storax and PADMA form dark smooth sweetness.
Patchouli, vetiver, cedar, nagarmotha, incense, opoponax, moss and transparent woods provide depth.
Ambrofix/Ambrox, three-way amberwoods, oud-suede-smoke traces and differentiated musks create controlled force.
hedonic_tuning: Spice is temperature-coded, not simply increased.
Lavender is floralized and sweetened from below so it avoids camphor and soap.
Licorice is a layered dark texture rather than one anise molecule.
Amberwood pressure is split among three materials to avoid scratch and fatigue.

missing_chemical_impact.function: Nutmeg warmth in multi-temperature spice crown
missing_chemical_impact.why_not_redundant: Cardamom and cinnamon cover coolness and heat but not nutmeg's dry, warm, slightly woody-spicy middle temperature.
missing_chemical_impact.loss_if_omitted: The spice crown becomes binary and less rounded.
missing_chemical_impact.overdose_failure: Culinary potpourri, dusty spice or woody dryness.
missing_chemical_impact.exact_comparison: Cinnamon-cardamom control versus +nutmeg at 0.5×/1×/1.5× in the grapefruit-lavender chassis.
missing_chemical_impact.owned_functional_coverage: Cardamom EO; cassia cinnamon available as a different material

missing_chemical_impact.candidate: Cinnamomum zeylanicum bark oil / exact Dior-compatible cinnamon comparator
missing_chemical_impact.why_not_redundant: Owned cassia is chemically and sensorially different and cannot be silently renamed Ceylon cinnamon.
missing_chemical_impact.loss_if_omitted: Heat may be harsher, more cinnamaldehydic and less nuanced.
missing_chemical_impact.overdose_failure: Candle, potpourri, burning spice and irritation risk.
missing_chemical_impact.exact_comparison: Cassia 1%, Ceylon 1% and no-cinnamon controls at equal cinnamic registration; safety remains separately gated.
missing_chemical_impact.owned_functional_coverage: Cinnamon Cassia Blume EO can be prepared at 1%, but is non-equivalent
missing_chemical_impact.purchase_or_prepare: Acquire only for exact target work; otherwise disclose cassia.

missing_chemical_impact.why_not_redundant: High-altitude lavender provides aromatic function, but cannot establish the non-camphor, floral, vanilla-coumarin facets Dior attributes to the selected Nyons blend.
missing_chemical_impact.loss_if_omitted: Lavender can read generic, soapier or more camphoraceous.
missing_chemical_impact.overdose_failure: Soap, camphor, medicinal dryness or fougère cliché.
missing_chemical_impact.exact_comparison: Owned high-altitude lavender versus AOP Nyons lot at equal perceived lavender intensity, with cardamom and rich woods fixed.
missing_chemical_impact.owned_functional_coverage: Lavender EO High Altitude; linalool/linalyl acetate; coumarin/vanillin
missing_chemical_impact.purchase_or_prepare: High value for target fidelity, not required for a concept study.

missing_chemical_impact.why_not_redundant: Anise EO alone is not a complete licorice accord; the function requires anisic, coumarinic, vanillic, immortelle, benzoin and dark-trace integration.
missing_chemical_impact.loss_if_omitted: The rich woods lose their velvety dark sweetness and recognizable Elixir shadow.
missing_chemical_impact.overdose_failure: Cough syrup, anise candy or medicinal sweetness.
missing_chemical_impact.exact_comparison: No licorice, anise-only and full prepared accord at equal anisic registration in the rich-wood base.
missing_chemical_impact.owned_functional_coverage: All listed accord building blocks are owned
missing_chemical_impact.purchase_or_prepare: Prepare with a receipt and test standalone first.

interaction_map.expected_effect: Bitter grapefruit makes hot/cool spice feel explosive and dry.
Cardamom coolness and cinnamon/nutmeg heat frame a floral lavender center.
Vanilla-coumarin facets descend from lavender into licorice.
Dark sweetness lacquers patchouli, vetiver and cedar.
Natural/root woods gain projection from distributed amberwoods.
Oud, suede, smoke and animalic traces create depth and danger.
interaction_map.physical_test: Dark-shadow block omission and trace ladder.

interaction_map.expected_effect: Musks polish pressure and improve wearability without erasing detail.
Bitter grapefruit should recur as a dry edge inside licorice.
Phenolic smoke can amplify spice harshness.
interaction_map.physical_test: No-smoke versus full shadow at equal load.

test_plan.primary_comparison: Full Red Moon Licorice versus no-licorice, anise-only, no-dark-shadow, and multi-temperature spice controls.
test_plan.reference_gate: Current Elixir reference plus nutmeg and exact cinnamon/lavender comparators for full fidelity.

temporal_test.replication: Two non-consecutive days; matched application geometry
temporal_test.core_time_question: Does grapefruit-spice relay through lavender to licorice-rich woods without medicinal collapse?
temporal_test.instrumental_lane: HS-SPME-GC-MS at 0/30 min/2 h/8 h on sealed vial and blotter; static and dynamic data remain separate
temporal_test.sensory_lane: Coded descriptive time-intensity plus hard-defect checklist
temporal_test.thermodynamic_inputs: Exact stock amounts, ethanol/water matrix, temperature, substrate, dose area, vapor pressure, activity-coefficient model/version
